points.t: A patient on **methotrexate, ciclosporin, a biologic or a JAK inhibitor** needs a prescription, vaccine, antibiotic or advice.
Targeted blockade of **TNF, IL-17, IL-23, IL-4/13 or JAK** signalling, or broad immunosuppression.
Specialist-initiated (NICE TAs); shared-care monitoring; **no live vaccines**; check every new drug (**MTX + trimethoprim**).
Serious infection, **TB reactivation**, **methotrexate toxicity**, VTE and MACE with JAK inhibitors (MHRA 2023).

cause.lead: Target the cytokine that drives the disease.
points: **Psoriasis = IL-23 / Th17 axis**: dendritic cells release IL-23 → Th17 cells make **IL-17A/F** → keratinocyte overgrowth and neutrophils; TNF-α amplifies.
Blocking IL-23 (p19) or IL-17 gives **PASI 90** in most; IL-17 blockade works fastest.
**Atopic eczema = Th2**: IL-4 and IL-13 weaken the barrier and drive IgE and itch; IL-31 is an itch cytokine.
**Dupilumab** blocks IL-4Rα (IL-4 + IL-13); tralokinumab / lebrikizumab block IL-13; **JAK inhibitors** block many cytokines inside the cell.

visuals.caption: The psoriasis loop: a dendritic cell signals to a T cell, which releases cytokines (such as IL-17) that make keratinocytes multiply and draw in neutrophils. Biologic antibodies intercept these signals.
visuals.alt: Schematic of immune cells and cytokines in psoriatic skin

features.lead: Know the classes, so you recognise them on a hospital-only record.
points: **TNF-α**: adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab, certolizumab. **IL-12/23**: ustekinumab.
**IL-23 (p19)**: guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab. **IL-17**: secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab, brodalumab.
**Eczema**: dupilumab; tralokinumab, lebrikizumab; JAK inhibitors abrocitinib, upadacitinib, baricitinib.
**Oral small molecules**: apremilast, dimethyl fumarate, deucravacitinib (TYK2).
**Conventional**: methotrexate, ciclosporin, acitretin; azathioprine, mycophenolate off-label in eczema.
**PASI ≥ 10 and DLQI > 10** after conventional systemic and phototherapy failed or unsuitable.
Moderate–severe (e.g. EASI ≥ 16, DLQI ≥ 10) after ≥ 1 conventional systemic.
TB (IGRA ± CXR), hepatitis B/C, HIV, VZV, pregnancy; **live vaccines ≥ 4 weeks before**.

cards.name: TNF inhibitors
cards.clue: TB reactivation, serious infection, paradoxical PPP, demyelination, heart failure.

cards.name: IL-17 inhibitors
cards.clue: **Candidiasis**, new or worse **IBD**: avoid in IBD.

cards.name: Dupilumab
cards.clue: Ocular surface disease, facial redness, eosinophilia, oral HSV.

cards.name: JAK inhibitors
cards.clue: MHRA 2023: **MACE, malignancy, VTE, serious infection**; caution ≥ 65, smokers, CV risk.

cards.name: Ciclosporin
cards.clue: **BP and creatinine**: reduce or stop if creatinine rises > 25–30%.

manage.lead: Primary care: record, protect, monitor; never initiate biologics or JAK inhibitors.

points: Flag the hospital-only drug, dose interval and homecare provider.
Check interactions with **every** new prescription.
Lower threshold to review and treat; **hold the next dose** in significant infection and contact the team.
Fever or serious infection: same-day assessment.
Inactivated (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal) encouraged; **no live vaccines**.
Shingles: non-live **Shingrix**, not Zostavax.
**Once WEEKLY**; record the **day of the week** (MHRA 2020); patient card.
**Folic acid 5 mg once weekly** on a different day.
Bloods per BSR/BAD shared care and local protocol.

visuals.caption: Methotrexate is taken on one chosen day each week; folic acid is taken on a different day, never the methotrexate day. Write the day on the prescription.
visuals.alt: Week of tiles with methotrexate on one day and folic acid on another

limits.t: Checks on JAKi, TNF-i, previous PUVA or ciclosporin.

items.t: Fever, sore throat, **mouth ulcers or bruising** on methotrexate: same-day FBC; withhold until reviewed.
Serious infection or **TB symptoms** on a biologic or JAKi: urgent assessment, contact team.
Cough or breathlessness on MTX (pneumonitis); chest pain or VTE symptoms on JAKi.
New IBD symptoms on IL-17 inhibitor; eye pain or visual loss on dupilumab.

pearls.t: Red eye on dupilumab = **ocular surface disease** until proven otherwise: tell dermatology.
IL-17 inhibitor + bloody diarrhoea = **IBD** until proven otherwise.
‘Methotrexate: one day a week, write the day down, no trimethoprim.’

quiz.q: Which antibiotic must never be co-prescribed with methotrexate?
Shingles vaccine for a patient on a JAK inhibitor?
quiz.a: The non-live recombinant vaccine (Shingrix), not live Zostavax.
PASI ≥ 10 and DLQI > 10 after conventional systemic failure or unsuitability.
Suspect new or worsening IBD: assess and contact the team.
